definition: In statistics, iterated conditional modes is a deterministic algorithm for obtaining a configuration of a local maximum of the joint probability of a Markov random field.
details: It does this by iteratively maximizing the probability of each variable conditioned on the rest.

explainer.lead: Iterated conditional modes finds a local maximum of a Markov random field's joint probability by updating one variable at a time. It matters as a simple deterministic alternative to sampling for such models.

tiers.eli5: Like tuning a radio one knob at a time: hold everything else fixed, set each knob to its best position, and repeat until nothing improves.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run ICM to get a quick deterministic configuration for MRF inference, but it easily settles in a poor local maximum, so results depend on the starting configuration.
tiers.paperLevel: Iteratively maximizes the conditional probability of each variable given the rest, yielding a configuration at a local maximum of the joint probability. Being a local, deterministic method, it carries no guarantee of finding a global optimum.

explainer.example: In image denoising with a Markov random field, each pixel label is set to its most probable value given all neighbors, sweeping pixels repeatedly until labels stop changing.
